title: LeanForth check report, schema version 0.5
description: What `leanforth check --snapshot FILE --json` prints: one JSON text, then a line feed. Version 0.4's report (schemas/check-report-0.4.schema.json) of a development run (ADR 0012 E8, ADR 0020 D4): the verdicts a checked-environment snapshot holds, published again from it and not re-checked in this run, labelled on every declaration with where its verdict comes from. A final run, which reads no snapshot, keeps writing version 0.4. Saved verdicts support no claim: a final run re-checks everything from the export (the owner's answer to OQ-3).
$comment: Plan task 6.2.5, step SN3; a [format] decision for the owner. Version 0.3 (schemas/check-report-0.3.schema.json, kept unchanged) without the member label, which the owner withdrew on 2026-11-12 (a [format] change the owner decided: results carry no label), at the top and on each accepted declaration. The members of 0.4, with export null (no export is read), read.phase snapshot for a refused snapshot, and mode, snapshot and each declaration's provenance.

export.description: Escaped display text of the export's file name as the command line gave it, when an export was checked against the snapshot (plan task 6.2.5, step SN4); null: a run of a snapshot alone reads no export (its identity is in snapshot.export).

manifest.description: checked: the export was read only if it matched EXPORT.manifest.json (the default); not-checked: --no-manifest.

mode.description: development: a run of saved results, for development and research only (ADR 0012 E8); a final run writes report 0.4.

snapshot.description: The snapshot read, or null when it was refused before its identity was read.

fuel.description: Fuel each declaration's check starts with (--fuel).

dependencyPool.description: The room the run's dependency pool starts with; it grows (not a limit since plan task 6.2.0).

strictAxioms.description: true with --strict-axioms: a NOT PROVED declaration makes the exit status 6; false by default, when NOT PROVED keeps Lean's exit status (owner, 2026-11-04).

anyLeanVersion.description: Present, true, only with --any-lean-version: the export's metadata could name any exporter and Lean version of format 3.1.0 (an optional member added within version 0.1, 2026-11-10; a report without the option is as before).

memoryPerCheck.description: Present only with --memory-per-check MB: the megabytes (of 2^20 bytes) each declaration's check may hold in scratch; a check that would pass it is full (diagnostic 101; core/scratch-meter.fs). LeanForth's own resource limit, never a Lean verdict (an optional member added within version 0.2, 2026-11-11; a report without the option is as before).

exportMeta.description: Present only when the export's metadata names another exporter or Lean version than the pinned lean4export 3.1.0 and Lean 4.35.0 (possible only with --any-lean-version), and the export was staged: what it names, in the shape of the export's own meta record, each text as escaped display text (see `export`). The verdicts are still those of Lean 4.35.0's rules. An optional member added within version 0.1 (2026-11-10).

run.description: The run's outcome: ok when every declaration's slot ended final; not-run when the export was not read.

stopped.description: true when the run stopped on an internal fault (a check threw, or publishing failed): the declaration where it stopped is invalid, and those after it are not checked.

declarations.description: Every declaration in input order, when the run's environment could be read; none otherwise.

counts.description: The declarations by verdict; null when no verdict could be read.

input.description: The input as fed to the checker; null when it was not.

exitStatus.description: The command's exit status: 0 all accepted (NOT PROVED ones too, as Lean, unless settings.strictAxioms), 1 something rejected, 2 unsupported or unknown, 3 a resource limit, 4 malformed input, 5 an internal fault, 6 all accepted but some NOT PROVED (only with settings.strictAxioms); the most severe of 5, 4, 1, 3, 2, 6, 0 wins.

allOf.description: An export that was not read was not checked.
Declarations are listed exactly when they are counted.
A run that ended ok made every slot final: no declaration is not-checked.

Exit status 0 only when the run ended ok, did not stop, listed at least one declaration and every declaration was accepted or skipped (an unsafe or partial declaration, which Lean's replay skips: status 0 as Lean): every other count is 0, and every fuel is known. NOT PROVED ones keep Lean's status 0 by default.
Under --strict-axioms, exit status 0 only when no declaration is NOT PROVED.
Exit status 6 only under --strict-axioms, when every declaration was accepted and at least one is NOT PROVED.
A rejected declaration makes the status 1 unless a worse one (4, 5) wins.
An invalid declaration makes the status 4, or 5.
A declaration not checked means the run stopped on an internal fault.
A run that stopped on an internal fault has status 5 and did not end ok; one that never ran did not stop.

allAccepted.description: Counts in which every declaration was accepted or skipped: at least one, and none with another verdict.

verdict.description: accepted for a slot made final with outcome ok; skipped for a rejected slot of an unsafe or partial declaration, which Lean's replay skips unchecked and nothing can use (plan task 5.2.7); another outcome's name for any other final slot, and invalid for one whose check began but did not end final; not-checked for one the run never reached.

name.description: Escaped display text, not the name's bytes: a declaration's name as the text output shows it (src/cli/name-text.fs; docs/user/COMMAND_LINE.md, Names): Lean's Name.toString, with every component that is not an identifier between « and », and inside it what the text rule bans and » as \u{X}, a byte that is not UTF-8 as \x{X}, a backslash as \\. Two declarations can show the same text; index identifies a declaration.

read.description: Reading the export: its outcome and, for a failure, the phase that failed (open: the file did not open; stage: the importer stage, with the line, field and reason of the NDJSON reader or the manifest check, line 0 for the manifest and for sealing; feed: giving the stage to the checker, with the number of the expression or declaration where it stopped). For a run of a snapshot: snapshot, the snapshot refused, with the reason (the section or check) and at the record (a slot, or a tier record), or null.

diagnostic.description: What the failed check recorded: the reason code and its name (docs/programming/DIAGNOSTICS.md), the site (module and word, or empty), its two numbers, and the step reached: check-block's for a member of an inductive block, else check-declaration's.

index.description: The declaration's position in the input, from 0: what identifies it (its name is display text).

axiomBits.description: The axiom set read from the accepted slot, as bits (src/core/axiom-allowlist.fs, version 1): 1 propext, 2 Classical.choice, 4 Quot.sound, each with Lean's statement, and 8 any other axiom; 0 for none.

notProved.description: true for an accepted declaration that depends on an axiom outside the allowlist (bit 8): Lean's verdict, labelled NOT PROVED and never counted as proved (owner, 2026-11-04).

notProvedBy.description: With notProved true only: the axioms outside the allowlist the declaration depends on, in file order (none named when no axiom declaration carries the bit).

provenance.description: Where the verdict comes from (ADR 0020 D4, OQ-3): snapshot, taken from the snapshot and not re-checked in this run; uses-snapshot, checked in this run but resting on the snapshot's results; checked, checked in this run. With --snapshot-stale-ok and a snapshot of an older verdict version (ADR 0020 amendment 3): stale-snapshot and uses-stale-snapshot instead, never this build's verdict.

fuel.description: Fuel the declaration's check used: exact for an accepted one (with that budget it is accepted, with one less not) and the budget for an exhausted one; 0 for a member of an inductive block after its first, whose check is the first's, and for one not checked; null when not known, for a check that ended with no fuel left without running out (a failed inference gives its counter up).

skipped.description: Unsafe or partial declarations, which Lean's replay skips (plan task 5.2.7).

notProved.description: Accepted declarations that are NOT PROVED (counted among accepted too).

total.description: Fuel used by every check of the run whose use is known.

unknown.description: Declarations whose fuel used is not known (null fuel).

top.description: The declarations that used the most fuel, most first, those of equal fuel in input order; none that used none.

input.description: The input as fed: declarations, term nodes, levels and constant references in the checker's stores, and names in the stage.

spent.description: A task's microseconds in a run with workers: busy, and waiting.

measured.description: Not deterministic, or how the run was made rather than what it found: wall and CPU time of each phase and of the whole run so far, in microseconds (null on a host without clocks; 0 for a phase that did not run, and a wall time of 0, not a negative one, when the host clock was set back during the phase), the peak resident memory of the process in bytes (VmHWM of /proc/self/status; null where the host does not give it), the bytes of heap blocks the stage held (null when nothing was staged) and the engine bin/leanforth ran. The engine is here, not in settings, so that the same check on either engine gives the same report but for this member.

save.description: Present only with --resources, when a snapshot was to be written (--save-snapshot): the time the save took (an optional member added within versions 0.4 and 0.5, 2026-11-24; a report without --resources is as before).

engine.description: The last part of the file name of the Forth engine bin/leanforth ran (LEANFORTH_ENGINE), as escaped display text: gforth, Gforth's checking engine, by default; gforth-fast with --fast. null when not known (not run by bin/leanforth).

declarationMicroseconds.description: Present only with --resources, on a host with clocks, when the declarations are listed: the wall microseconds each declaration's own check took, in file order (entry i is declaration i), timed in the context that ran it, so that the slowest declarations can be listed by time and not only by fuel; 0 for one not checked in this run (a block's member after its first, whose check the first's covers; one taken from a snapshot; one after the run stopped; a check that threw). In a run with workers they add up to a little less than the workers' busy time. An optional member added within versions 0.4 and 0.5, 2026-11-25; a report without --resources is as before.

workers.description: Present only with --resources, when the check ran with workers (--jobs N above 1, or the default of 4; owner, 2026-11-23) on a host with clocks, in microseconds: the plan's and the jobs' run's wall and CPU time, both within the check phase; in the jobs' run, the driving task's busy time (handing out, publishing, rolling back) and waiting time (for a job to end); each worker's busy time (its checks) and waiting time (the rest of the jobs' run, when it had no job), in the order the workers were made; and all workers' busy and waiting time together. A worker replaced after a THROW counts its replacement's time only. An optional member added within versions 0.4 and 0.5, 2026-11-24; a report without --resources, or of a run without workers, is as before.

snapshot.description: The snapshot read (ADR 0020 D3): its file, its identity (the SHA-256 of its header, which holds every section's SHA-256), its format and verdict versions, the export it was written from, the manifest's SHA-256 (null when no manifest was checked), its base (null: a base snapshot), the layers loaded on it and the information text of the build that wrote it (a JSON text, shown, never compared).

file.description: Escaped display text of the file name as the command line gave it.

verdictVersion.description: The snapshot's verdict version (kernel/verdict-version.fs): a snapshot of another verdict version than this build's is refused, unless --snapshot-stale-ok lets an older one load (stale).

stale.description: null, or with --snapshot-stale-ok when the snapshot or a layer has an older verdict version (ADR 0020 amendment 3): this build's verdict version and how many results were taken from the stale snapshots; those are never this build's verdicts.

layers.description: Each layer loaded on this base snapshot, in order (ADR 0020 amendment 1, F5): its file, identity (its header's SHA-256), the export it was written from and its base's identity (this snapshot's sha256). Empty for a base alone.

import.description: With an export checked against the snapshot (plan task 6.2.5, step SN4; ADR 0020 D5): how many of the export's declarations were taken from the snapshot (the import rule I1) and checked in this run, and how many share a name with a declaration of the snapshot but the content of none; null when no export was read or the snapshot was refused. checked counts the declarations whose verdict this run gave (fewer than those not taken when the run stopped).
